reachability: Every new life is made at Yale in New Haven at one of five US banks. Since 2026-10-16 creation's Before Yale can keep an account at a bank in the country the student lived in before Yale (systems/homeaccount.ts): a Berlin-raised student keeps a current account at Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, Postbank, ING or Berliner Sparkasse (each 'conditional', docs/research/banking/home-accounts.json), and can press Close It on it once another current account is primary (bank.close_current). So Germany's closing fee is reached in play now, which the last pass's result didn't say. Cancel It on a home account isn't (it was opened before Yale, and every cooling-off has ended by the first day of term), and no German bank closes a home account of its own accord (only Barclays does, homeTerms), so homeCloses at a German bank is a fixture.

sources.rule: BGB § 675h(3): “Im Fall der Kündigung sind regelmäßig erhobene Entgelte nur anteilig bis zum Zeitpunkt der Beendigung des Vertrags zu entrichten. Im Voraus gezahlte Entgelte, die auf die Zeit nach Beendigung des Vertrags fallen, sind anteilig zu erstatten.” § 675h(4): no charge may be agreed for the termination itself.
sources.effective: 13 January 2018, in the wording of the Act implementing the Second Payment Services Directive of 17 July 2017 (BGBl. I S. 2446), as dejure.org gives the version

sources.rule: BGB § 357b(2): on withdrawal from a distance contract for a financial service the consumer owes Wertersatz “für die vom Unternehmer bis zum Widerruf erbrachte Dienstleistung”, where told beforehand and agreeing to the service starting within the period.

Deutsche Bank's price list, Persönliche Konten: “Die Kontoführung im Eröffnungsmonat ist kostenfrei. Die Kontoabrechnung erfolgt vierteljährlich.”; db AktivKonto “Monatlicher Grundpreis (Kontoführung) 6,90 EUR”; “Auflösung der Kontoverbindung kostenfrei”.

Commerzbank's price list: GiroKonto “Kontoführung Monatspreis 4,90 EUR”, free with €50,000 checked on the month's last banking day, “Sofern die Vermögenswerte den Mindestwert von 50.000 EUR unterschritten haben, wird der Monatspreis mit dem nächstfolgenden Kontoabschluss berechnet”; its distance-selling information (Stand 19.06.2026) books “Kontoführungsentgelte monatlich” and says Wertersatz on a withdrawal can mean paying “die vertraglichen Zahlungsverpflichtungen für den Zeitraum bis zum Widerruf”.
Postbank's price list: Giro plus “Grundpreis pro Monat” €5.90 with €1,000 paid in in the calendar month, €6.90 otherwise; “Rechnungsabschlussperiode bei Girokonten vierteljährlich”.

ING's Girokonto conditions: free with €1,000 paid in in the calendar month or under 28, else “4,90 € monatlich”, “Belastung des monatlichen Entgelts im Folgemonat”; “Vierteljährlicher Rechnungsabschluss”.

Berliner Sparkasse's price list: Giro Digital “Kontoführung pro Monat 4,95 EUR”; footnote 45, on yearly fees paid ahead (the Sparkassen-Card's €12.00 a year): “Im Fall der vorzeitigen Auflösung des Vertragsverhältnisses vor dem Jahresende erfolgt eine anteilige Erstattung vorausbezahlter Entgelte gemäß § 675 h III BGB.”

items.item: Germany's month's fee on a close (brief 09 section 4; the last pass's banking.1.pro-rata, left to the owner).
items.requirement: On a close, a German current account owes its regularly charged monthly fee only pro rata to the end of the contract (BGB § 675h(3)); on a cancellation in the cooling-off period, Wertersatz for the service given up to the withdrawal (§ 357b(2)), on the contract's price. The months already ended in the quarter are owed whole (each was served whole); the closing month's share by the days the account was open in it, through the closing day, of the month's days, in exact cents; nothing is refunded where nothing was paid ahead. Balanced ledger entries. The amount and its explanation shown before the player presses Close It or Cancel It. Month boundaries, leap years, the closing date, insufficient funds, a repeated attempt, save and load, and twins in one jump and day by day.
items.currentBehavior: settleFees (src/engine/systems/banking.ts:521-530) and closingFeesOf (:543-545) charge the quarter so far (feesDue) and the whole of this month's fee (feeFor at the month's start), whatever day the account closes. Reproduced (scratchpad banking/base/tests/probe-banking.test.ts, run 2026-10-16): a Berlin-raised student keeping Deutsche Bank, at Yale from 24 August 2026, presses Close It on her AktivKonto on Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 9 AM and is charged “Closing fees: AktivKonto” −690 (€6.90), where 14 of October's 31 days are €3.12. Nothing on Your Banks or Your Accounts Over Time says what closing charges before it's pressed: the line under Close It (src/ui/bank/BankMoves.tsx:163) says only a refusal, and Cancel It's (src/ui/bank/BankAccountLife.tsx:116) says “less the fees it owes” without the figure. Fees collected ahead: none at a German bank in SLATE: feeFor's monthly fee accrues at each month's end into feesDue and posts at the quarter's closing (banking.ts:629-642), so every fee posted is for a month already served.

items.plan: One breakdown in banking.ts (closingFeesDue): the quarter's months kept (feesDue, and feesDueHeld in the bank's money), and this month's share: feeFor's figure (in the bank's own money first where the account is kept in another), times the days the account was open in the month through the closing day (from its opening day where it opened that month), over the month's days, rounded half up to the cent in integers; none once the month's end has accrued the month (a close after 11 PM on its last day). settleFees and closingFeesOf read it, so Close It's, Cancel It's and the bank's own close's refusals and charges are one figure. Its words (closingFeesWords) under Close It on Your Banks and under Cancel It, before either is pressed. The guide's Another Bank and Keeping An Account entries say it. Tests in tests/remaining-09-banking.test.ts, played on a Berlin-raised student keeping Deutsche Bank: the figure on the screen, pressed, posted once, the ledger balanced, a reload, twins jump and day by day, the month's first day, its last before and after the month's end, a quarter's end, February in 2027 and 2028, insufficient funds then paid in, a second press. The three tests the audit cites change with dated comments and new titles, recorded in docs/verification/pipeline/inputs/renames.json.

items.item: Found while checking month boundaries: a close after the month's end on its last day charges that month twice.
items.requirement: Each month's fee is charged once (the ledger's own rule: funds never duplicate).
items.currentBehavior: The month's end runs at 11 PM on the last day and adds the month's fee to feesDue (banking.ts:629-631); settleFees then adds feeFor for the same month again (:523-524). Reproduced: the same Berlin-raised student closing her AktivKonto at 11:30 PM on Saturday 31 October 2026 is charged “Closing fees: AktivKonto” −1,380 (€13.80) for October alone; the quarter's closing on 30 September had posted August and September.
items.plan: The share is none once the month's end for the closing month has run (now at or past 11 PM on its last day): the month is in feesDue already, whole.

items.item: What the last pass found and left: homeCloses re-settles fees on each daily retry at a bank with quarterly fees (systems/abroad.ts).
items.requirement: A fee is charged once (the ledger's rule); and BGB § 675h(3): fees are owed only to the end of the contract, so once a bank's notice has run out nothing more accrues on the account it keeps open only to be paid.
items.currentBehavior: homeCloses (abroad.ts:501-547) settles interest, overdraft interest and fees on every attempt (:509), and an overdrawn account is tried again each day (:516-520): settleFees charges the month's fee again each day, and the month's end goes on accruing. Reproduced on a fixture (Deutsche Bank given Barclays' kind of rule, 60 days' notice, TEST SETUP): from Friday 23 October 2026 “Closing fees: AktivKonto” −690 every morning, eight times by 30 October. Reachable now? No: only Barclays closes a home account (docs/research/banking/home-accounts.json: gb-barclays kept false), and Barclays settles monthly with no fee (closesQuarterly false).
